title: Flame Wrap editor export with explicit low VP9 quantizer over default 4:2:0 (controlled parity experiment)
scope: Same retained production editor/Host chain and project family as the failed default 4:2:0 run; explicit native VP9 quantizer policy only. Confirms divergence sits in encoder quantization policy, not renderer or timing. Default-policy failure remains open and unchanged.

source.projection: subset; full receipt, video, project and pins retained at source root

ui.scope: Actual production editor textboxes, attached-session history tasks, real Host graph/record and full presentation canvas pixels. Not raw native pixels or UI-created animation channels.

export.format: explicit opaque WebM VP9 4:2:0 native quantizer control (not the default quality policy)

lifecycle.retainedConsole: Two optional preset 404s, ten preview AbortError cancellation logs from the UI history flow, one Canvas2D readback advisory; retained, not a zero-console claim

interpretation: Same renderer, same project family, same thresholds and failing frame: the only changed input is the encoder quantization policy. Explicit VP9 quantizer 8 (4:2:0, native quantizer path) passes all three reference frames including the previously failing ticks=40000. The default-quality 4:2:0 failure is therefore attributable to encoder quantization configuration, not pre-encode pixels, timing or the Flame Wrap renderer. Default policy remains unfixed; this does not relax any threshold or substitute for fixing it.
boundary: Explicit quantizer path acceptance only; the default 4:2:0 quality policy failure, Electron host, hardware GPU, installed plugin and alpha master remain outside this evidence.
